description: A female Central Connecticut State University police officer filed a federal lawsuit in March 2019 against the university, alleging that fellow campus officer Curtis Lollar raped her three times — twice while on duty in the summer of 2014 and once at his home in 2016. According to the complaint, when she reported the incidents she was publicly shamed, denied backup on calls, and required to keep working alongside Lollar for nearly a year. The suit alleged the department fostered an environment in which sexual harassment and assault were the norm, hired officers despite disciplinary red flags, and failed to investigate officers' alleged sexual harassment of students; an independent Shipman & Goodwin investigation of the department reached similar conclusions. Lollar was fired in September 2018. CCSU agreed to pay the officer a $1.75 million settlement, reported in August 2020.
notes: Filed before 2021; included because seed dataset covers it. Seed year hint was 2018 (the year Lollar was fired); reporting indicates the lawsuit was filed in March 2019.
